applies_to: Earlier EVAPCO eco-Air air-cooled and adiabatic fluid coolers and condensers with EC fans and the pCO-type controller.
summary: Earlier eco-Air controller generation whose native protocol is Modbus RTU; BACnet needs an optional expansion card (pCONet RS-485 card for MS/TP, pcoWeb Ethernet card for BACnet IP). Object instances use large numbers (BV 100009, AV 200001 and so on) and temperatures are scaled in tenths of a degree. Points cover enable, unit state, temperatures, setpoints, fan limits, pre-cooling stages and per-fan alarms.
notes: Temperatures are reported in 0.1 °F and pressure in 0.1 psi steps, per the units column.
This is the older guide; newer eco-Air PLC panels use the COMM24 object list starting at instance 0.
Per-fan alarm and communication points only apply to fitted fans.

source.title: EVAPCO Controller User's Manual Addendum - Communications Guide EC Fan Edition

integration.summary: Fit the BACnet expansion card (pCONet for MS/TP or pcoWeb for IP), set its parameters through the controller BIOS menu, then enable the unit via BV 100009. Read AV 200001 unit state, AV 100001 outlet temperature and BV 100026 common alarm, and write AV 100004 for the process setpoint.

minimum_points.name: Enable Unit
minimum_points.why: BMS enable when configured for BMS enable

minimum_points.name: Actual Unit State
minimum_points.why: Running, off by alarm, off by BMS, scheduler or local

integration.enable: Write BV 100009 Enable Unit = 1; it only applies when the unit is configured to be enabled via BMS. AV 200001 = 4 means off via Modbus/BACnet.
setup: BACnet requires an optional card: pCONet (BACnet MS/TP) or pcoWeb (BACnet IP / Modbus TCP); Modbus RTU on J25 is always available.
Card settings are changed from the BIOS menu: hold ALARM + ENTER for 3 s, Other Information > pcoWeb/Net Config, then pCOWeb or pCONet settings.
Default parameters are on page 1 of the panel wiring diagram.
gotchas: Writable parameters are stored in the PLC's non-volatile memory, rated for about 100,000 writes; never write them cyclically.
Points marked for adiabatic units (pre-cooling valves, flush, wet-stage timers) can be ignored on dry-only units.
Scaled values: divide 0.1 °F / 0.1 psi points by 10 if your front end does not apply the scale.
